overview: Black answers 4.d5 with ...b5, offering a pawn to build a large pawn centre. After 5.dxe6 fxe6 6.cxb5 d5 Black has e6/d5 pawns and play on the f-file, while White tries to keep the extra pawn or the Rubinstein 5.e4 line. Black plays for the centre and development rather than quick material.

white_ideas.idea: Accept the pawn and consolidate with dxe6 and cxb5
Keep the extra pawn and aim for a quiet development with g3 and Bg2
Play the Rubinstein 5.e4 to keep d5

black_ideas.idea: Build the e6/d5 centre after ...fxe6 and ...d5
Use the open f-file and bishop on b7 for pressure
Regain the pawn with ...a6 or ...Bb7 pressure

typical_structures.structure: Black pawns on e6 and d5 with White queenside pawn majority

character.notes: A countergambit that gives away a pawn for centre control and piece activity; both sides take risks.

gambit.notes: A pawn is offered that the opponent can keep.

soundness.notes: Reputable and sound in practice, played by strong players now and then.

structure.notes: Black gets a central duo with the f-file open; asymmetrical centre.

approach.notes: Respectable but not a main choice.

level.notes: The pawn centre plans have to be handled well.

plan_phrases: regain the pawn with piece pressure

sublines_that_differ.name: Rubinstein Variation
sublines_that_differ.how: White keeps d5 and a centre instead of dxe6.

character.reason: A pawn-offering countergambit with unbalanced play.

gambit.reason: Black offers the b5 pawn for the centre and can be kept.

soundness.reason: Playable at club and strong levels.

structure.reason: Asymmetric centre with the open f-file for Black.

approach.reason: Reputable if rare, not a system.

level.reason: Plans are clear but pawn-centre handling takes experience.

plans.reason: Black builds a centre and activity for the pawn.
